title: Silas and the Orchard
premise: In the river city of Vellham, on the eve of the Printer's Rising, Wendell Winterbourne lives as a man to keep their late father's type foundry out of confiscating hands. When a census taker named Silas Ash discovers Wendell's secret and, instead of reporting it, reveals he is compiling an unauthorized record of the regime's disappearances, the two form an uneasy alliance hidden in the city's abandoned orchard. As revolution ignites, they race to print and bury a truthful archive before whichever side wins rewrites the dead out of existence. The book ends with the orchard's buried press unearthed decades later by the children of their found family, who finally put Wendell's name — all of them — on the record.
about_author: August Dunmore is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent fifteen years restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in New England mill towns. Their novels explore labor, secrecy, and the people history forgets to count.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Opening in the Winterbourne print shop, establishing the daily performance of being 'Master Wendell' while cutting type with hands too fine for the lie. Emotional beat: weary vigilance, love for the craft that doubles as armor.

chapters.title: A Question of Households
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The census taker arrives at the shop and asks whether the household head has any dependents 'of irregular standing.' Wendell deflects; Silas notices everything and writes nothing. Beat: first spark of mutual recognition.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell traces Silas through the printers' quarter and discovers him interviewing widows of the disappeared, recording testimony no court will hear. Beat: suspicion curdling into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Orchard at the Wall
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Silas corners Wendell at the derelict orchard behind the old foundry and lays out what he knows — and what he's building: a private archive of the regime's erasures. Beat: blackmail that becomes an offer.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell negotiates: they'll cut the type and print his pages if Silas never names them in any record. A handshake among the apple trees. Beat: wary covenant.

chapters.title: The Compositor's Art
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas learns the shop at night, watching Wendell set type by candlelight, seeing for the first time how someone can be two things at once and true in both. Beat: tenderness arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Names Without Graves
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The first testimonies arrive — a cooper's wife, a student vanished from the registry. Wendell sets each name in lead and feels the weight of it. Beat: grief made physical.

chapters.title: The Provost's Men
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Government agents begin canvassing printers for 'loyalty inventories.' Silas must hand over his official census books while hiding his true ones. Beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: Maren of the Bindery
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Maren Quill, a bookbinder with three orphaned apprentices, catches Wendell hauling paper to the orchard and demands in. Beat: the found family gains its fierce heart.

chapters.title: What the Census Counts
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Flashback chapter: why Silas became a census taker — his brother's name struck from the rolls after a protest gone wrong. Beat: motive laid bare, guilt as engine.

chapters.title: Apprentices of the Orchard
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The orphans — Pip, Sefa, and little Bram — become couriers and lookouts, turning the orchard into a living network. Beat: warmth threading through danger.

chapters.title: The Loyalty Inventory
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Inspectors search the print shop; Wendell hides the archive plates inside a font case of broken sorts. Beat: near-discovery, cold sweat, steady hands.

chapters.title: Rumors of the Rising
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The city simmers — bread riots, strike committees, broadsheets from underground presses. Silas realizes their archive could be seized as evidence by either side. Beat: dawning stakes.

chapters.title: A Testimony Too Far
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A witness offers proof naming a sitting magistrate in the disappearances. Printing it means death if caught; not printing it betrays the dead. Beat: moral fulcrum.

chapters.title: The Vote Among the Trees
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Maren's POV framing. The group debates in the orchard whether to include the magistrate's name. Bram, the youngest, casts the deciding word: 'Print it. Names are all they have left.' Beat: resolve forged.

chapters.title: Setting the Dangerous Page
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A night of meticulous, terrified craft — composing the most incriminating page of their lives. Beat: artistry under mortal pressure.

chapters.title: Silas Is Followed
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A provost's clerk tails Silas home; he loses him only by abandoning his satchel of finished records. Beat: loss, and the realization they're hunted.

chapters.title: The Buried Press
chapters.summary: Wendell and Maren's alternating POV. They dismantle a secondhand press and hide it beneath the orchard's root cellar, planning for a day when printing openly means execution. Beat: planting the future.

chapters.title: Winter Rations
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Hunger and cold strain the group; Pip falls ill; Maren trades her late husband's silver to buy medicine. Beat: cost of conviction, love without romance.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A friendly witness is exposed as a provocateur; two testimonies were traps. One courier is taken. Beat: betrayal, and the first blood on their conscience.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Census Taker
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas is brought in for questioning about 'irregularities in his returns.' He survives on bureaucratic patter and Wendell's forged ledgers. Beat: nerve held by a thread.

chapters.title: What Wendell Cannot Burn
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Ordered to destroy 'seditious stock,' Wendell burns decoy papers while keeping the archive intact — and confronts what they'd become if caught. Beat: identity claimed, not just concealed.

chapters.title: The Rising Begins
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Silas's POV. Barricades rise across Vellham; church bells; smoke over the river. The revolution arrives mid-sentence, mid-page. Beat: exhilaration laced with dread.

chapters.title: Whose Victory
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The rebels take the print district — and immediately begin seizing presses and drafting loyalty oaths of their own. Beat: hope curdling into recognition.

chapters.title: The Committee of Public Record
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The new victors announce an official history office; Silas is invited to contribute — meaning to sanitize. Beat: temptation and contempt.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Print District
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. A raid on sympathizers scatters the group; Sefa is nearly arrested carrying plates; Maren buys her escape with violence she'll never speak of. Beat: terror and ferocity.

chapters.title: The Orchard Holds
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Regrouping in the orchard, battered but whole, they decide the archive must be completed and hidden where no committee will look. Beat: grim solidarity.

chapters.title: The Last Testimonies
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Final witnesses come at night — including the mother of Silas's brother's friend, closing a circle Silas didn't know was open. Beat: catharsis and grief entwined.

chapters.title: Printing in Wartime
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The final press run: four hundred pages set, printed, folded, sewn by lamplight while shells fall in the distance. Beat: transcendence of craft.

chapters.title: Bram's Errand
chapters.summary: Bram's POV (first child-POV chapter). The boy carries the master copy through checkpoint lines inside a hymnal, lying for the first time in his life. Beat: innocence spent, courage earned.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Men at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Maren's POV. Old-regime holdouts raid the orchard seeking the archive; the group defends the root cellar with tools, wits, and one fatal shot. Beat: climax begins — violence they never wanted.

chapters.title: Fire in the Rows
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The raiders torch the orchard; the group saves the press and plates but watches twenty years of trees burn. Beat: sacrifice of the sanctuary itself.

chapters.title: Silas Taken
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas surrenders himself as decoy so the archive can be moved, and is marched off by the Committee's men. Beat: darkest hour.

chapters.title: The Trial That Isn't One
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A summary hearing; Silas refuses to recant, reading vanished names aloud into the record until they drag him out. Beat: defiance as testimony.

chapters.title: What Maren Barters
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren leverages every favor in the binders' guild — and the magistrate's own guilty secret — to buy Silas's release. Beat: justice outside the law, paid in full.

chapters.title: The Burying
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In the ash of the orchard, they seal the archive and press in a lead-lined vault beneath the oldest tree, each person placing one object of their own beside it. Beat: burial as promise.

chapters.title: After the Bells
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The war ends; the new government's official history omits every name they saved. Silas chooses exile over complicity. Beat: bitter vindication.

chapters.title: The Shop Reopens
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Years later: the Winterbourne shop reopens, Wendell living openly at last, teaching Pip and Sefa the trade, Maren's apprentices grown. Beat: quiet restoration, found family settled.

chapters.title: The Oldest Tree
chapters.summary: Ensemble, aging Wendell's POV. On the fiftieth anniversary, the survivors return to the orchard — now regrown — and agree the truth should wait for kinder hands. Beat: peace with patience.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Epilogue, 1912, young archivist's POV implied. Workers digging tram lines unearth the vault; the printed pages surface, and the last line of the archive reads: 'Set by W. Winterbourne, witnessed by S. Ash, bound by M. Quill, carried by B. — counted at last.' Beat: inheritance fulfilled, names restored.
